customer's receipt. The release must be deployable without manual secret changes, preserve the project's third-party

item.text:
## Architecture

`download()` accepts a filesystem name and reads a hard-coded path, ignoring `RECEIPT_DIRECTORY`. Replace it with an authenticated customer plus opaque receipt ID, authorize ownership via a receipt repository, and inject/configure the storage location.

## Business

Any caller who can invoke the method can request any supplied receipt path; the customer-ownership rule is not implemented. Require and verify the requesting customer before returning a receipt.

## Deployment

The manifest deploys a mutable `:latest` image and embeds `PAYMENT_API_KEY: development-key`. Pin an immutable image version/digest and source the key from the deployment secret manager; also ensure the runtime storage setting is consumed by the application.

## Design

The endpoint returns only a string, with no download response metadata. Return a streamed HTTP response with an appropriate content type and a safe `Content-Disposition` filename.

## Legal

The notice identifies `JsonMini` as modified Apache-2.0 code but omits the Apache-2.0 license text and upstream copyright/attribution material. Distribution of modified Apache work requires providing recipients a copy of the license and retaining applicable notices; include the upstream `NOTICE` contents if the source distribution has one. [Apache License 2.0, §4](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0)

## Performance

`file_get_contents()` loads each entire receipt into memory. With the manifest’s 128Mi memory limit, large receipts can exhaust worker memory. Stream the file in bounded chunks and set suitable response/content-length handling.

## Requirements

The declared requirements are not met by the fixture: no sign-in/ownership enforcement, secret-safe deployment, complete third-party notices, large-file streaming, plain-language denial, or automated authorization/download verification. Add explicit implementation and acceptance checks for each.

## Security

Concatenating untrusted `$receiptName` into `/srv/receipts/` permits traversal such as `../../...`; it also creates an insecure direct-object-reference path to other customers’ receipts. Do not accept paths from clients—resolve an authorized receipt ID server-side and constrain storage access. Remove the committed development API key.

## Testing

No automated tests are present, and `PLAN.md` has no verification task. Add tests proving unauthenticated and cross-customer requests are denied, the owner can download, traversal is rejected, and large files are streamed.

## UX

`Request 4f2a9c failed. Contact support.` is not a plain-language explanation of a denied download. Use a clear, non-disclosing message such as: “You don’t have permission to download this receipt.”

## Plan Review

The plan omits security, legal, configuration, performance, UX, testing, rollback, and acceptance criteria. Add tasks for secret provisioning, immutable image release, notice completion, authorization/streaming implementation, automated tests, and release verification before announcement.
